references.name: Dreamflow
references.steal: Tri-pane with three live-synced surfaces — agent chat, visual canvas, full code editor; edit any one, the other two update. No-lock-in file-system access: the visual layer edits real project files.
references.why: The closest structural sibling (Flutter-native, AI-first). Its tri-surface sync is the bar: the flows canvas must reflect the actual built target, not a stale mock.

references.name: FlutterFlow

shot.caption: editor anatomy — widget tree + canvas + properties

references.steal: Page-list rail + canvas + properties inspector — the classic three-column builder anatomy. Design Library panel: global colors, type scales, component styles in one place.
references.why: The incumbent the indie-dev evaluator already knows. Matching its editor anatomy makes app-box legible in 30 seconds; the flows canvas is the differentiator it does not have.

references.name: v0 / Lovable / Bolt.new
references.steal: Split view: prompt/chat thread left, live running preview right — the now-standard AI-builder layout. Generation timeline: versioned checkpoints per prompt, roll back to any prior render.
references.why: The chat-to-app trio defines the entry expectation; app-box’s gate history (approve/reject/regenerate) should look like v0’s versioned checkpoints.

references.name: MagicPath

shot.caption: prompt input on the multiplayer canvas

references.steal: Prompt-to-canvas, not prompt-to-chat — generated screens land as tiles on the infinite canvas; the canvas is the document. Multi-page flow generation: one prompt, a connected sequence of screens.
references.why: The strongest existing proof of app-box’s core layout — AI is for generation, hands are for refinement.

references.name: Linear
references.steal: Triage Inbox as the gate queue — pending approvals never pollute the main pipeline view. Sub-issue trees with rolled-up status: per-surface traceability, each surface carrying its own gate/check status.
references.why: Proves a dense data tool can feel calm. Its status semantics map almost 1:1 onto gate states (queued → running → awaiting approval → approved/rejected).

references.name: Vercel Deployment Checks
references.steal: Deployment Checks = app-box’s gates: named, blocking conditions as a checklist with running/succeeded/failed states. Check row: name, status icon, duration, expandable output, re-run affordance.
references.why: The best quality-gate-as-UI pattern in the industry — checks-as-UI is the founder’s gate model verbatim.

references.name: GitHub Actions
references.steal: The pattern every developer already knows — app-box wins by being familiar here, not novel. Job graph + expandable per-step logs.
references.why: Familiarity is the feature: the pipeline run page should read instantly to anyone who has watched an Actions run.

references.name: Sentry

shot.caption: issue detail — stack frames to file:line

references.steal: Issue stream rows: severity color bar, culprit (file:function), event count, first/last seen. Map to SARIF: severity chip, rule ID, file:line chip, occurrence count across runs.
references.why: app-box’s SARIF findings need Sentry’s discipline — aggregated, deduplicated, ranked by severity — or the founder drowns in linter noise.

references.name: GitHub Mobile
references.steal: Push for a deployment-review deep-links straight into the exact review dialog — Approve / Reject, no navigation detour. Per-notification-category scheduling.
references.why: The founder’s existing mental model for "walked away, phone buzzes, approve the deploy" — the canonical push → approve/reject loop.

references.name: Linear mobile
references.steal: Triage inbox as the home screen: a queue of items each demanding exactly one decision. Frosted-glass material with discipline — depth behind navigation, never behind content.
references.why: The current craft benchmark for dev-tool mobile — the direct answer to the "too mediocre" bar.

references.name: Raycast

shot.caption: raycast.com home — the macOS polish ceiling

references.steal: Command-bar ergonomics: every action reachable by fuzzy search, keyboard-first, visible shortcuts — the macOS shell should open on a command bar ("approve", "retry gate", "open preview").
references.why: The macOS polish ceiling, now with a phone companion — dense lists that still breathe.

references.name: Tailscale device approval

shot.caption: device approval — the admin trust gate

references.steal: New device connects but is inert until approved — a newly paired phone can view but cannot Approve/Reject until an already-paired device confirms it.
references.why: Answers the threat QR alone doesn’t: human-confirms-new-device is the difference between "paired" and "trusted to mint approvals".

Evan is the founder mapping the client brief; Michelle is the indie-dev evaluator — her 20-minute first-run is an R1 must.
